Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Communications Engineering and 16 years in biotechnology and software development, my background equips me with a technical and leadership perspective on Scrum values. My 12 years of Scrum experience shape my research into how Scrum practices enhance software quality. This expertise might lead to assumptions that agile techniques inherently foster quality, creating biases towards validating their effectiveness. My background may drive me to prioritize engineering-focused interpretations and value practical applications, possibly overlooking non-technical dimensions. Thus, my positionality informs my research approach, shaping my coding choices and interpretation of data to reflect deeper insights into the interplay between Scrum practices and software quality.

init_codebook.definition: QA's involvement from the start enhances understanding and reduces bugs.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of QA participating early in the development process.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions of QA involvement only at the testing phase.
typical_examples: QA is part of one dev team.
atypical_examples: QA comes and gets involved directly with the product owner.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Involving QA early is integral to advancing software quality by reducing bugs.

init_codebook.definition: A team-oriented culture improves software quality through constant communication and shared knowledge.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of collaboration and team efforts in software development.
exclusion_criteria: Solo development activities.
typical_examples: Team collaborate more and knowledge flow better.
atypical_examples: Scrum helps peers get ideas on how to structure your code.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Collaboration within teams aligns with Scrum principles to improve software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Ongoing feedback from various stakeholders enhances software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Involvement of client or team feedback processes.
exclusion_criteria: Initial requirement specifications without further input.
typical_examples: The client can see what you do after each sprint.
atypical_examples: Feedback from users, you know, and also encourages TDD.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Feedback loops are a key aspect of Scrum practices that ensure continuous quality improvement.

init_codebook.definition: Implementing automated and manual testing processes to ensure code quality.
inclusion_criteria: Descriptions of automated testing and consistent QA practices.
exclusion_criteria: General comments on quality without mentioning testing.
typical_examples: You need to have automated regression tests.
atypical_examples: We have automation test cases running on a regular basis.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Testing strategies directly relate to achieving high software quality as proposed in Scrum frameworks.

init_codebook.definition: A safe environment enables team members to take initiatives and improve software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of psychological safety and its effects on work quality.
exclusion_criteria: Strict hierarchical mention without psychological elements.
typical_examples: If you have a lot of psychological fear of failure, you have ineffective ideas.
atypical_examples: Having that first meeting includes everybody.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Psychological safety is important for team dynamics and improving software quality through Scrum values.

init_codebook.definition: Team members take ownership and accountability for their work, impacting software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mention of accountability or personal responsibility in team settings.
exclusion_criteria: Cases where responsibilities are unclear or distributed inefficiently.
typical_examples: Everyone takes responsibility and has accountability for the project.
atypical_examples: Accountability boosts the motivation to meet expectations on quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Accountability aligns with Scrum roles impacting software quality control.

Role_Team.positionality: With a background as a Software Developer holding a Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology and 30 years in the IT industry, including 8 years of Scrum experience, I approach analyzing Scrum's impact on software quality from a veteran perspective. My extensive experience may lead to a pragmatic lens in assessing research, heavily favoring proven, systematic approaches. I acknowledge a potential bias toward methodologies that align with my deep-seated knowledge and principles of IT. This positionality might guide me to emphasize frameworks and outcomes consistent with my personal and professional history, potentially affecting how I interpret and prioritize qualitative data while addressing how Scrum's values foster software quality.

init_codebook.definition: QA involvement from the start is crucial for understanding requirements and reducing bugs.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions QA's early involvement.
Discusses QA's understanding of requirements.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions QA only during later testing phases.
Focuses on roles unrelated to requirements understanding.
typical_examples: They come into picture from day one.
atypical_examples: The QA comes and gets involved directly with the product owner and not just the development team.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Illustrates how early QA involvement aligns with Scrum values to advance software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Early QA involvement is seen as a method to ensure requirement clarity and quality.

init_codebook.definition: Enhanced collaboration within teams leads to better software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions how collaboration impacts software quality.
Highlights teamwork in improving quality.
exclusion_criteria: Focuses on individual work without team collaboration.
Describes teamwork unrelated to quality.
typical_examples: Collaboration helps better quality by facilitating intensive exchange of information.
atypical_examples: Collaborate with the product owner to improve understanding and quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights how Scrum's emphasis on collaboration supports achieving software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Collaborative practices are central to improving quality through shared understanding.

init_codebook.definition: Team members' accountability leads to higher commitment to quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions accountability as a driver for quality.
Discusses impact of feeling accountable on quality.
exclusion_criteria: Lacks connection between accountability and quality.
Focuses on non-related motivations.
typical_examples: People feel accountable, they take ownership of the work they do and its quality.
atypical_examples: When the culture is that everyone is accountable for everyone, developers feel accountable to meet the team’s expectations on quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows how Scrum promotes accountability, which enhances software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Accountability is interconnected with Scrum's principles of collective responsibility.

init_codebook.definition: Frequent feedback and iterations lead to continuous improvements in quality.
inclusion_criteria: Describes the role of feedback in quality improvement.
Mentions iterative processes improving quality.
exclusion_criteria: Lacks mention of feedback or iterative improvements.
Focuses on feedback unrelated to quality.
typical_examples: Iterative inspection process allowed us to correct, adjust and at the end deliver functionality that meet the client’s needs.
atypical_examples: Providing iterations with frequent feedback helps align with client expectations and improve quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explains how iterative processes in Scrum ensure ongoing quality enhancement.
init_codebook.notes: Iterative feedback loops are integral to the Agile process, adapting to requirements.

init_codebook.definition: An environment that empowers developers improves motivation and quality outcomes.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions empowerment as an influence on quality.
Describes motivated work environments.
exclusion_criteria: Lacks evidence of empowerment affecting quality.
Focuses entirely on external motivations.
typical_examples: When developers are empowered, they make their own decisions on the quality of their work.
atypical_examples: Empowered environment drives better software design and coding practices.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Reveals how empowerment aligns with Scrum principles to enhance software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Developer empowerment is linked to increased commitment and quality improvements.

Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Data Science, 30 years of software development experience in electronic manufacturing, and 7 years of Scrum experience, my research is deeply influenced by my technical background. This expertise shapes my perspective on the research exploring the impact of Scrum on software quality, potentially leading me to favor quantitative outcomes or technological efficiencies. My biases may incline me toward valuing structured data over qualitative insights. Consequently, my interpretations and coding decisions might prioritize measurable results or frameworks efficiently aligned with Scrum principles, thus potentially overlooking more nuanced, human-centered aspects of software quality.

init_codebook.definition: The team learns from each other to improve code quality.

exclusion_criteria: Statements about individual learning or personal improvement without collaboration
typical_examples: People learn from each other’s how to write better code.
atypical_examples: Developers cross-check each other's work during peer review.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code shows how Scrum practices encourage mutual learning, contributing to better software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Reflects the interactive aspect of Scrum in facilitating knowledge sharing.

init_codebook.definition: QA contributes from the beginning, enhancing the clarity and testing of requirements.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of QA being involved from the start of the project or sprint planning
exclusion_criteria: QA involvement limited to the testing phase only
typical_examples: QA are involved from day one.
atypical_examples: QA giving feedback during requirement gathering.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Early QA involvement ensures comprehensive test planning and reduces bugs, supporting software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Emphasizes the shift towards integrated roles in Agile.

init_codebook.definition: Clear and open channels of communication contribute to software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Statements highlighting the role of transparency in improving clarity and reducing errors
exclusion_criteria: Statements not directly related to communication or team interaction
typical_examples: Transparency leads to openness, leading to fewer bugs.
atypical_examples: Regular updates between team members to align on goals.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Transparent communication ensures that all team members have a clear understanding, promoting higher software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Highlights communication as a foundational element of Agile methodologies.

init_codebook.definition: Iterative processes help refine and enforce product quality by allowing continuous feedback.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of iteration cycles and continuous feedback improving quality
exclusion_criteria: Descriptions of non-iterative processes
typical_examples: Iteration cycles provide regular feedback, improving overall quality.
atypical_examples: Clients reviewing each iteration cycle outcome.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Iterative improvement allows Scrum to enhance quality through frequent refinements.
init_codebook.notes: Shows how incremental progress linked to iterative reviews supports quality assurance.

init_codebook.definition: Encouraging a team-oriented approach to responsibility for software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Statements referring to shared ownership and responsibility
exclusion_criteria: Mentions where accountability is solely with one individual
typical_examples: You cannot have someone to blame. It’s a team’s responsibility.
atypical_examples: Developers and QAs share responsibility for outcomes.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Collective accountability promotes thorough quality checks, thus enhancing software quality.
init_codebook.notes: Reflects Agile's emphasis on collaborative efforts over individual blame.

Despite the slightly different code names, the shared understanding is that collaboration aids in knowledge sharing and quality improvement, aligning with Scrum principles.

agreements.code: Role Accountability / Accountability Drives Quality / Team Accountability

agreements.reason: All roles discuss accountability as a driver or essential component for maintaining high software quality. Each version of this code suggests the importance of team members or entire teams taking responsibility for their work.

codebook.definition: QA's involvement from the start enhances understanding and reduces bugs.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of QA being involved from the start of the project or sprint planning.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions of QA involvement only at the testing phase.
typical_examples: QA is part of one dev team.
QA are involved from day one.
atypical_examples: QA comes and gets involved directly with the product owner.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Involving QA early is integral to advancing software quality by reducing bugs.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'Role of QA', addressing redundancy across roles with shared emphasis on early QA involvement.

codebook.definition: A team-oriented culture improves software quality through constant communication and shared knowledge.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of collaboration and team efforts in software development.
exclusion_criteria: Solo development activities.
typical_examples: Team collaborate more and knowledge flow better.
atypical_examples: Scrum helps peers get ideas on how to structure your code.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Collaboration within teams aligns with Scrum principles to improve software quality.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'Collaboration Enhances Quality' to unify overlapping interpretations across different roles.

codebook.definition: Ongoing feedback from various stakeholders enhances software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Involvement of client or team feedback processes.
exclusion_criteria: Initial requirement specifications without further input.
typical_examples: The client can see what you do after each sprint.
atypical_examples: Feedback from users, you know, and also encourages TDD.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Feedback loops are a key aspect of Scrum practices that ensure continuous quality improvement.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'Iterative Feedback and Improvement' and 'Iterative Development for Quality'. Emphasizing unified interpretation of feedback and iteration as quality drivers.

codebook.definition: Team members take ownership and accountability for their work, impacting software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mention of accountability or personal responsibility in team settings.
exclusion_criteria: Cases where responsibilities are unclear or distributed inefficiently.
typical_examples: Everyone takes responsibility and has accountability for the project.
atypical_examples: Accountability boosts the motivation to meet expectations on quality.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Accountability aligns with Scrum roles impacting software quality control.
codebook.notes: Aligned from 'Accountability Drives Quality' and 'Team Accountability', reflecting cross-role consensus on its importance for quality.

codebook.definition: A safe environment enables team members to take initiatives and improve software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of psychological safety and its effects on work quality.
exclusion_criteria: Strict hierarchical mention without psychological elements.
typical_examples: If you have a lot of psychological fear of failure, you have ineffective ideas.
atypical_examples: Having that first meeting includes everybody.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Psychological safety is important for team dynamics and improving software quality through Scrum values.
codebook.notes: Retained for its distinct emphasis on team environment, supported by cross-role discussions.

codebook.definition: Clear and open channels of communication contribute to software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Statements highlighting the role of transparency in improving clarity and reducing errors.
exclusion_criteria: Statements not directly related to communication or team interaction.
typical_examples: Transparency leads to openness, leading to fewer bugs.
atypical_examples: Regular updates between team members to align on goals.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Transparent communication ensures that all team members have a clear understanding, promoting higher software quality.
codebook.notes: Retained uniquely for its focus on communication, distinct from general collaboration.

codebook.definition: The team learns from each other to improve code quality.
inclusion_criteria: Descriptions of team members learning from one another or collaborating to improve.
exclusion_criteria: Statements about individual learning or personal improvement without collaboration.
typical_examples: People learn from each other’s how to write better code.
atypical_examples: Developers cross-check each other's work during peer review.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This code shows how Scrum practices encourage mutual learning, contributing to better software quality.
codebook.notes: Retained for its specific emphasis on educational enhancement within teams.

codebook.definition: Implementing automated and manual testing processes to ensure code quality.
inclusion_criteria: Descriptions of automated testing and consistent QA practices.
exclusion_criteria: General comments on quality without mentioning testing.
typical_examples: You need to have automated regression tests.
atypical_examples: We have automation test cases running on a regular basis.
codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Testing strategies directly relate to achieving high software quality as proposed in Scrum frameworks.
codebook.notes: Retained to highlight the critical role of explicit testing in quality assurance, as discussed across roles.
